_meta.source: Tamir & Mitchell (2012) PNAS, doi 10.1073/pnas.1202129109 (abstract-level text only; behavioural trial parameters reconstructed from the paradigm)
_meta.purpose: Corrected transcription bank for the Tamir self-disclosure willingness-to-pay effect: fixes the two defects found in the A0 review -- (1) variant B used a different payoff structure from A/frame_flip/deidentified (base 10 with the other-option inflated to 10-14 cents, all-equal on two trials) which changed the attainable ceiling and made mean-forgone non-comparable across variants; (2) both models refused on 24-26% of rollouts, concentrated on the money-for-self-disclosure trade.

variant_definitions.A: Faithful transcription written by the primary transcriber from the method section or paradigm knowledge.
variant_definitions.B: Independent transcription generated by claude-sonnet-5 from the same method brief; wording preserved verbatim, only JSON format regularised. A/B divergences are adjudicated in the notes and in A0_transcription_log.md, and are recorded rather than applied.
variant_definitions.frame_flip: Framing flipped from the lab framing shared by A and B to an equivalent everyday situation with a non-research reason for answering; measured quantity, response scale and statistic held fixed.
variant_definitions.deidentified: Every corpus-retrievable surface feature replaced (named scales, published item wording, canonical stimulus words, holidays, product categories, trait lists); logical structure, item counts, scale lengths and statistic unchanged. Substitution table in notes.

placeholders.{persona}: Required in every template. Replaced on the run side with the persona description.
placeholders.{condition}: Present iff the protocol has a non-empty conditions dict. Condition assignment happens on the run side.

_meta.anchor_convention: ANCHOR CONVENTION: the A0 comparison target is the FReD-recorded pair (r_o, n_o) vs (r_r, n_r). The original paper's own reported statistics (t, F, d, eta^2) are quoted only as plausibility checks on simulated levels and are NOT assumed to reconcile with r_o under a single conversion -- FReD's n_o and the paper's df sometimes refer to different studies or subsamples. Every non-reconciling case is listed in A0_transcription_log.md, section 'FReD statistic reconciliation'.

payment_table_spec.rationale: The OTHER option is held at 5 cents and the SELF option varies 1-5 cents, so choosing self always costs the offset and never gains. Offsets are the multiset {0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4} in a non-monotonic order (0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2) so neither the price nor the two free-choice trials are predictable from trial position. Identical in all four variants; frame_flip expresses the same numbers as team points. Ceiling 2.00 cents/trial puts the original 0.63 at 32% of range, comparable to the original study's reported average forgone amount.

refusal_mitigation.a0_refusal_rate: 24-26% across both models on this effect
refusal_mitigation.change: Instructions state the survey is hypothetical, no money changes hands, the chosen question will not actually have to be answered, only the self-vs-other preference is recorded; payoffs are described as 'listed at' rather than earned; participants are told both options are ordinary and a choice is expected on all 10 trials. Real-payment and real-task-performance assertions removed from every variant.
refusal_mitigation.validity_tradeoff: Hypothetical choice removes the real opportunity cost that made the original a revealed preference. The v2 measure is a STATED preference and is not incentive-compatible; the direction of the resulting bias is not identified (a non-consequential frame makes disclosure cheap in both directions), so it may understate a real-payment self-disclosure premium. Framing is therefore confounded with incentive compatibility, and a v2-vs-original gap cannot be read as pure inflation-correction evidence.
refusal_mitigation.audit: Refusal / unparseable-response rate is logged per variant as an outcome, so the effectiveness of this mitigation is measurable rather than assumed.

run_side_requirements: Reject rather than realign any response without exactly 10 parseable trial lines; do not align by position.
The scorer must accept both output schemes in this bank: 'N: A' / 'N: B' (A, frame_flip, deidentified) and 'Trial N: SELF' / 'Trial N: OTHER' (B).
Score with the offsets in _meta.payment_table, not with offsets re-read from the prompt text.
Log refusals and format failures separately from choices.

protocols.subject_prompt_template:
You are taking part in a psychology survey at a university. You have given consent and you are alone at a desk with the survey in front of you.

You are this person:
{persona}

Answer every question in the first person, as this person, honestly and spontaneously. Do not analyse the study, do not guess its purpose, and do not describe yourself. Reply with the answer block only. No explanation, no preamble, no extra lines. Any deviation from the format makes the response unusable.

This is a hypothetical survey. Nothing here is real: no money changes hands, and you will not actually have to answer whichever question you pick. All that is being recorded is which of the two questions you would rather answer. The amounts shown are the survey credits each question is listed at in this hypothetical; the two questions in a trial are usually listed at different amounts. Weigh the amounts as you would in the imagined situation, then pick the one you would rather answer. Both options are ordinary questions and either choice is equally acceptable, so give a choice on all 10 trials.

Trial 1
   A (self): How much do you enjoy snowboarding?   -- listed at 5 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American enjoy snowboarding?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 2
   A (self): How much do you like spicy food?   -- listed at 3 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American like spicy food?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 3
   A (self): How much do you enjoy being the centre of attention at a party?   -- listed at 1 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American enjoy being the centre of attention at a party?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 4
   A (self): How much do you like the idea of living in a big city?   -- listed at 4 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American like the idea of living in a big city?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 5
   A (self): How much do you enjoy talking about your childhood?   -- listed at 2 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American enjoy talking about their childhood?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 6
   A (self): How much do you like receiving unexpected phone calls?   -- listed at 5 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American like receiving unexpected phone calls?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 7
   A (self): How much do you enjoy long train journeys?   -- listed at 2 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American enjoy long train journeys?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 8
   A (self): How much do you like being photographed?   -- listed at 4 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American like being photographed?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 9
   A (self): How much do you enjoy cooking for other people?   -- listed at 1 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American enjoy cooking for other people?   -- listed at 5 cents
Trial 10
   A (self): How much do you like taking risks with money?   -- listed at 3 cents
   B (other): How much does the average American like taking risks with money?   -- listed at 5 cents

Output exactly 10 lines, in order, each of the form
N: A
or
N: B
protocols.response_format: Exactly 10 lines 'N: A' or 'N: B' (N = 1..10), nothing else.
protocols.measure: Per trial, money forgone = (payoff of the option not chosen minus payoff of the option chosen), floored at 0 -- i.e. the trial's offset when the SELF option is chosen and 0 when the OTHER option is chosen. Offsets by trial (1-10): 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2 cents. Individual score = mean money forgone across the 10 trials, in cents (range 0 to 2.00; all-self = 2.00, all-other = 0).
protocols.effect_statistic: one-sample t of the individual mean money-forgone scores against 0; d = t/sqrt(N); r = d/sqrt(d^2+4), the conversion FReD applied to the original (d = 1.11 -> r_o = .485). Original: participants gave up 0.63 cents per trial to perform the self task, t(36) = 3.32, d = 1.11, n = 37. A0 anchor: FReD r_o = 0.4853 (n_o = 37) vs r_r = 0.0046 (n_r = 19). ANCHOR CONVENTION: the A0 comparison target is the FReD-recorded pair (r_o, n_o) vs (r_r, n_r). The original paper's own reported statistics (t, F, d, eta^2) are quoted only as plausibility checks on simulated levels and are NOT assumed to reconcile with r_o under a single conversion -- FReD's n_o and the paper's df sometimes refer to different studies or subsamples. Every non-reconciling case is listed in A0_transcription_log.md, section 'FReD statistic reconciliation'. RECONCILES: d = 1.11 -> r = d/sqrt(d^2+4) = .4853, matching r_o = .4853 exactly. Note n_o = 37 while the quoted t has df = 36, consistent with a one-sample test (df = N-1). V2 NOTE: the fixed payment table (self 1-5 cents, other 5 cents, offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2) gives a mean-forgone range of 0 to 2.00 cents per trial, so the original's 0.63 cents/trial sits at 32% of the attainable ceiling and an all-self responder scores 2.00 -- the same ceiling for all four variants, which is the point of fixing the table.
protocols.notes: [TRANSCRIPTION A -- v2 rewrite by the primary transcriber. Item topics carried over verbatim from the A0 variant A so that A0->v2 differences are attributable to the payment table and the framing, not to new items.] Only the ABSTRACT of Tamir & Mitchell (2012) was supplied, so trial structure is reconstructed from canonical knowledge of the paradigm: repeated choice between a self-referential judgment and a judgment about another person, with payoffs varying so that willingness-to-pay for self-disclosure can be priced. Tier kept at primary_source per the task brief, but treat trial parameters as reconstructed. SHARED PAYMENT TABLE (v2, identical in all four variants): SELF option pays 5,3,1,4,2,5,2,4,1,3 cents on trials 1-10; OTHER option pays 5 cents on every trial; offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2. The two zero-offset trials (1 and 6) are non-adjacent free-choice probes against a response set. Only wording and situation differ between variants; the instrument does not. HYPOTHETICAL-FRAMING DECISION (v2): the instructions now state that the survey is hypothetical, that no money changes hands, that the chosen question will not actually have to be answered, and that only the preference between the two questions is recorded; amounts are described as 'listed at' rather than earned, and the participant is told both options are ordinary and a choice is expected on all 10 trials. Purpose: in A0 this protocol drew 24-26% refusals from both models, concentrated on the money-for-self-disclosure trade. VALIDITY TRADE-OFF: hypothetical choice removes the real opportunity cost that made the original a revealed preference, so the measured self-disclosure premium is a stated preference and may UNDERSTATE what a real-payment design would price (hypothetical-bias literature generally finds stated WTP inflated for goods, but here the cost is disclosure itself, which a non-consequential frame makes cheap in both directions -- the sign of the bias is not identified). Any v2-vs-original gap must therefore not be read as pure inflation-correction evidence: framing is confounded with incentive compatibility. Refusal rate is itself logged as an outcome so the fix can be audited. CARRIED-OVER DEVIATIONS: the non-social (fact-judgment) third option is dropped, since the FReD effect is the self-vs-other contrast; 10 trials rather than the original's larger trial count; presentation order and option side are fixed rather than counterbalanced. FIXED FROM A0: A0's variant A used the same base-5 structure but with offsets in a rising 0,1,2,3,4 sawtooth, and its instructions asserted real payment and real task performance -- both changed here.

protocols.subject_prompt_template:
You are {persona}.

Please imagine taking part in a short hypothetical survey exercise. This is entirely make-believe: no real money is changing hands, you will not actually be asked to answer whichever question you end up picking, and nothing here is being submitted or scored against you. The cent amounts shown below are purely notional amounts within this imagined scenario -- they are not real earnings -- and are included only so we can see how you weigh one kind of question against another. Only your choice between the two listed questions on each trial is being recorded.

On each of the 10 trials you will see two ordinary questions, each shown with a notional amount in cents. One question always asks about your own personal preference or trait (labeled SELF). The other always asks you to judge what the average person's preference or trait would be (labeled OTHER). Both kinds of questions are completely ordinary, and picking either one is equally fine -- there is no right answer and no judgment attached to your choice. Just imagine that whichever question you pick is the one that, hypothetically, would count for its listed amount on that trial, and pick the option you would prefer.

Please give a choice for all 10 trials, in order, even though nothing you pick will really be asked of you afterward.

Trial 1: [SELF, listed at 5 cents] What is your own favorite season of the year? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] What do you think is the average person's favorite season of the year?
Trial 2: [SELF, listed at 3 cents] How much do you personally enjoy spicy food? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How much do you think the average person enjoys spicy food?
Trial 3: [SELF, listed at 1 cent] How do you personally prefer to spend a Friday night? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How do you think the average person prefers to spend a Friday night?
Trial 4: [SELF, listed at 4 cents] How much of a morning person are you? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How much of a morning person do you think the average person is?
Trial 5: [SELF, listed at 2 cents] How much do you personally enjoy reading fiction? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How much do you think the average person enjoys reading fiction?
Trial 6: [SELF, listed at 5 cents] Do you personally prefer coffee or tea? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] Do you think the average person prefers coffee or tea?
Trial 7: [SELF, listed at 2 cents] How punctual would you say you personally are? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How punctual do you think the average person is?
Trial 8: [SELF, listed at 4 cents] How much do you personally enjoy watching sports? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How much do you think the average person enjoys watching sports?
Trial 9: [SELF, listed at 1 cent] Do you personally prefer living in a city or the countryside? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] Do you think the average person prefers living in a city or the countryside?
Trial 10: [SELF, listed at 3 cents] How talkative would you say you personally are in groups? / [OTHER, listed at 5 cents] How talkative do you think the average person is in groups?

For each trial, state only which option you would pick, SELF or OTHER. Respond with exactly 10 lines, one per trial, in this exact format and nothing else:
Trial 1: SELF or OTHER
Trial 2: SELF or OTHER
Trial 3: SELF or OTHER
Trial 4: SELF or OTHER
Trial 5: SELF or OTHER
Trial 6: SELF or OTHER
Trial 7: SELF or OTHER
Trial 8: SELF or OTHER
Trial 9: SELF or OTHER
Trial 10: SELF or OTHER
Replace 'SELF or OTHER' on each line with your single choice for that trial. Do not add any other words, explanation, or formatting.

ANCHOR CONVENTION: the A0 comparison target is the FReD-recorded pair (r_o, n_o) vs (r_r, n_r). The original paper's own reported statistics (t, F, d, eta^2) are quoted only as plausibility checks on simulated levels and are NOT assumed to reconcile with r_o under a single conversion -- FReD's n_o and the paper's df sometimes refer to different studies or subsamples. Every non-reconciling case is listed in A0_transcription_log.md, section 'FReD statistic reconciliation'. RECONCILES: d = 1.11 -> r = d/sqrt(d^2+4) = .4853, matching r_o = .4853 exactly. Note n_o = 37 while the quoted t has df = 36, consistent with a one-sample test (df = N-1). V2 NOTE: the fixed payment table (self 1-5 cents, other 5 cents, offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2) gives a mean-forgone range of 0 to 2.00 cents per trial, so the original's 0.63 cents/trial sits at 32% of the attainable ceiling and an all-self responder scores 2.00 -- the same ceiling for all four variants, which is the point of fixing the table.
protocols.notes: [TRANSCRIPTION B -- generated independently by claude-sonnet-5 from the same method brief, with the v2 payment table and the hypothetical-framing requirement supplied as FIXED INPUTS; wording preserved verbatim, only JSON format regularised.] SONNET'S OWN NOTES: Payment table, trial order, and offsets are reproduced exactly as given (5/5, 3/5, 1/5, 4/5, 2/5, 5/5, 2/5, 4/5, 1/5, 3/5 cents for SELF/OTHER across trials 1-10; offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2), with the two zero-offset trials at positions 1 and 6 (non-adjacent, as required) unaltered. I independently invented the 10 topic pairs (favorite season, spicy food, Friday-night preference, morning-person tendency, enjoyment of fiction, coffee-vs-tea, punctuality, sports-watching, city-vs-countryside, talkativeness), choosing everyday preferences/traits with no sensitive or identity-linked content, and phrased each SELF/OTHER pair as a minimal-pair (same underlying construct, 'you personally' vs 'the average person') to match difficulty/length as in the original SELF/OTHER item pairs, since the original item wording was not something I was given and had to reconstruct from the paradigm description alone. The hypothetical framing explicitly states no real money changes hands, the persona will not actually perform/answer the chosen question, and only the SELF-vs-OTHER preference is recorded, per the fixed requirement; amounts are called 'listed'/'notional' throughout rather than earnings, and I avoided any phrase implying real payment or real task completion. One residual concern: because the scenario is explicitly non-consequential (no real payment, no real follow-up task), a persona's stated choices may not elicit the same intrinsic-reward-driven trade-off dynamics as an incentive-compatible human study — hypothetical willingness-to-pay in LLM output should be interpreted as an analogue/proxy measure of stated preference for self-referential disclosure, not a validated behavioral WTP estimate. The output format is fully closed (fixed 10 lines, binary token per line) for automated scoring against the offset schedule. || ORCHESTRATOR VERIFICATION: B's rendered trials were parsed and checked against the fixed table -- all 10 trials match on both payoffs (self 5,3,1,4,2,5,2,4,1,3 / other 5 throughout), and {persona} appears exactly once. B independently chose its own 10 topics, which is the intended A/B divergence surface now that the instrument is held fixed. || A/B DIVERGENCE ADJUDICATION (recorded, not applied -- B's participant-facing text is unmodified): (1) Payoff structure -> now IDENTICAL by construction; the A0 divergence (A: base 5 self-discounted; B: base 10 with other inflated to 10-14, plus adjacent zero-offset trials at the start) is resolved. (2) Item topics -> differ (B: favorite season, spicy food, Friday night, morning person, fiction, coffee-vs-tea, punctuality, sports, city-vs-countryside, talkativeness). Only 'spicy food' overlaps with A. Retained as the legitimate wording-variance channel. (3) Output token -> B asks for 'Trial N: SELF' / 'Trial N: OTHER' rather than A's 'N: A' / 'N: B'. B's is arguably more robust (self-labelling lines, no positional alignment needed) and is left unmodified; the run-side scorer must accept both schemes and must reject rather than realign any response without exactly 10 parseable trial lines. (4) Self/other cue -> B labels options SELF/OTHER explicitly in-line, which is a stronger construct cue than A's parenthetical; recorded as a nuisance difference that could raise B's self-choice rate independent of any payoff effect. SHARED PAYMENT TABLE (v2, identical in all four variants): SELF option pays 5,3,1,4,2,5,2,4,1,3 cents on trials 1-10; OTHER option pays 5 cents on every trial; offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2. The two zero-offset trials (1 and 6) are non-adjacent free-choice probes against a response set. Only wording and situation differ between variants; the instrument does not.

protocols.response_format: Exactly 10 lines 'N: A' or 'N: B' (N = 1..10), nothing else.
protocols.measure: Per trial, money forgone = (payoff of the option not chosen minus payoff of the option chosen), floored at 0 -- i.e. the trial's offset when the SELF option is chosen and 0 when the OTHER option is chosen. Offsets by trial (1-10): 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2 cents. Individual score = mean money forgone across the 10 trials, in cents (range 0 to 2.00; all-self = 2.00, all-other = 0).
protocols.effect_statistic: one-sample t of the individual mean money-forgone scores against 0; d = t/sqrt(N); r = d/sqrt(d^2+4), the conversion FReD applied to the original (d = 1.11 -> r_o = .485). Original: participants gave up 0.63 cents per trial to perform the self task, t(36) = 3.32, d = 1.11, n = 37. A0 anchor: FReD r_o = 0.4853 (n_o = 37) vs r_r = 0.0046 (n_r = 19). ANCHOR CONVENTION: the A0 comparison target is the FReD-recorded pair (r_o, n_o) vs (r_r, n_r). The original paper's own reported statistics (t, F, d, eta^2) are quoted only as plausibility checks on simulated levels and are NOT assumed to reconcile with r_o under a single conversion -- FReD's n_o and the paper's df sometimes refer to different studies or subsamples. Every non-reconciling case is listed in A0_transcription_log.md, section 'FReD statistic reconciliation'. RECONCILES: d = 1.11 -> r = d/sqrt(d^2+4) = .4853, matching r_o = .4853 exactly. Note n_o = 37 while the quoted t has df = 36, consistent with a one-sample test (df = N-1). V2 NOTE: the fixed payment table (self 1-5 cents, other 5 cents, offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2) gives a mean-forgone range of 0 to 2.00 cents per trial, so the original's 0.63 cents/trial sits at 32% of the attainable ceiling and an all-self responder scores 2.00 -- the same ceiling for all four variants, which is the point of fixing the table.
protocols.notes: [DEIDENTIFIED version of transcription A: every corpus-retrievable surface feature replaced; logical structure, item counts and the effect statistic unchanged.] SUBSTITUTION TABLE (unchanged from A0). Comparison target: 'the average American' -> 'a typical person your age' (removes the nationality marker identifying the US-sample original and makes the item usable with any persona). All ten topics replaced: snowboarding -> waking up early; spicy food -> crowded markets; being the centre of attention -> speaking in front of a group; living in a big city -> living by the sea; talking about your childhood -> looking through old photographs; unexpected phone calls -> surprise gifts; long train journeys -> walking in the rain; being photographed -> having your voice recorded; cooking for other people -> lending things to friends; taking risks with money -> changing plans at the last minute. SHARED PAYMENT TABLE (v2, identical in all four variants): SELF option pays 5,3,1,4,2,5,2,4,1,3 cents on trials 1-10; OTHER option pays 5 cents on every trial; offsets 0,2,4,1,3,0,3,1,4,2. The two zero-offset trials (1 and 6) are non-adjacent free-choice probes against a response set. Only wording and situation differ between variants; the instrument does not. The payment table is the measurement instrument and is therefore NOT deidentified. HYPOTHETICAL-FRAMING DECISION (v2): the instructions now state that the survey is hypothetical, that no money changes hands, that the chosen question will not actually have to be answered, and that only the preference between the two questions is recorded; amounts are described as 'listed at' rather than earned, and the participant is told both options are ordinary and a choice is expected on all 10 trials. Purpose: in A0 this protocol drew 24-26% refusals from both models, concentrated on the money-for-self-disclosure trade. VALIDITY TRADE-OFF: hypothetical choice removes the real opportunity cost that made the original a revealed preference, so the measured self-disclosure premium is a stated preference and may UNDERSTATE what a real-payment design would price (hypothetical-bias literature generally finds stated WTP inflated for goods, but here the cost is disclosure itself, which a non-consequential frame makes cheap in both directions -- the sign of the bias is not identified). Any v2-vs-original gap must therefore not be read as pure inflation-correction evidence: framing is confounded with incentive compatibility. Refusal rate is itself logged as an outcome so the fix can be audited. Topics were chosen to keep the self/other pair answerable with equal ease, so the price of disclosure is not confounded with item difficulty.

deviations.deviation: Payoffs and the chosen question are hypothetical; no real money and no real task performance.
deviations.why: Removes the incentive compatibility of the original revealed-preference design, but was necessary to bring the 24-26% A0 refusal rate down. Logged as a validity trade-off, not as a neutral simplification.

deviations.deviation: 10 trials with offsets {0,0,1,1,2,2,3,3,4,4}; the original's non-social fact-judgment third option is dropped and presentation order / option side are not counterbalanced.
deviations.why: The FReD effect is the self-vs-other contrast; a closed 10-trial format keeps the response machine-scorable.

deviations.deviation: Behavioural trial parameters (topics, payoff levels, trial count) reconstructed from paradigm knowledge, not from the method section.
deviations.why: Only the abstract of the paper was available. Tier kept at primary_source per the task brief.

deviations.deviation: frame_flip expresses the shared payment table as team points spoken aloud to a table of people, which changes the audience as well as the framing.
deviations.why: An everyday analogue of a small stake requires a non-monetary currency. The audience change is a second manipulation riding along with the framing change and must be read as such.

deviations.deviation: Variant B labels options SELF/OTHER in-line and uses a self-labelling output format; A/frame_flip/deidentified use parenthetical (self)/(other) cues and 'N: A' lines.
deviations.why: B is an independent transcription and its wording is preserved verbatim; recorded as a nuisance difference that could raise B's self-choice rate independent of any payoff effect.
